newsitem.title: UK: CRICKET-ATHERTON TO BLAME FOR ENGLAND FAILURE, ILLINGWORTH SAYS.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-ATHERTON TO BLAME FOR ENGLAND FAILURE, ILLINGWORTH SAYS.

text.p: Mike Atherton's "lacklustre" captaincy was to blame for the England cricket team's failure against New Zealand, former captain and chairman of selectors Ray Illingworth said.
"His lacklustre, unimaginative captaincy, along with some awful bowling, lay at the heart of another alarming tour debacle," Illingworth said in an interview published on Wednesday.
"If this carries on there will be no alternative to replacing him as captain," he told The Express newspaper.
England had looked set to win in Auckland when they reduced New Zealand to 105 for eight at lunch on Tuesday.
But New Zealand snatched a draw after Nathan Astle and Danny Morrison produced a last-wicket stand of 106, a record for New Zealand in tests against England.
"It was...an incredible outcome and Atherton's own errors of judgement and leadership were vividly evident," Illingworth said.
His words were echoed by another former England captain Bob Willis, who with Peter Willey set the highest test-saving last-wicket stand of 117, against West Indies in 1980.
"The side should have been captained better by Atherton," Willis told the Daily Star newspaper. "He was found wanting as far as I am concerned."
In 38 tests as captain, Atherton has won only eight times. England's last win overseas was in Adelaide two years ago and they have drawn six and lost two of their last eight tests.

Illingworth said: "They all have talent but if they can't knuckle down others have to be given a chance," he said. "That applies to the captain too. There comes a time when someone else must be given a go."
